newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China starts main work on Lingao nuclear plant.
newsitem.headline: China starts main work on Lingao nuclear plant.

text.p: China has started construction on the main structure of the Lingao Nuclear Power Station in southern Guangdong province, the Lingao Nuclear Power Co Ltd said in a statement on Thursday.
Chinese vice-premier Wu Bangguo symbolically started up a concrete mixer to mark the official start of work, the company said, but did not elaborate.
The US$4 billion plant will use more foreign capital than any other current China power project, the statement said, adding the financing was arranged through the State Development Bank of China.
The plant, located 1.2 km (0.7 miles) from the operational Daya Bay nuclear plant, will be equipped with four pressurised water reactors of 1,000 megawatts each, it said.
The first unit will be put into commercial operation by July 2002, while the second unit will be operational by March 2003, the statement said.
The French engineering group Framatome supplied the main components for the nuclear plant, while Electricite de France (EDF) provided consultancy services, the Chinese company said.
